_clock: Every 'start'/'end' below is written in the clock named by the shot's 'clock' field. 'broker' means the engine's own MT5 server timestamps — the same strings that appear in the trace and in data/XAUUSD_M15.csv. capture_tv.py resolves broker->UTC by measuring OHLC agreement, never by a hardcoded constant. Do not hand-convert times in this file.

month-fill.description: CH-monthly-tv-coverage-h4-recon: the two spans of the corpus month with NO TradingView capture of any kind (Jul 7-14, Aug 1-6). Wide M15 windows for OHLC/clock reconciliation coverage — deliberately NOT framed for candle-by-candle legibility, because the reconciliation reads TradingView bars from the widget API, not from pixels.

month-complete.description: CH-xauusd-tv-odds: the LAST four M15 spans of the corpus month with no TradingView capture, closing coverage from 1,241/2,116 bars (58.6%) to ~100% so a month-wide agreement rate has a complete denominator. Edges deliberately OVERLAP the existing shots 07/08/04/06 — scripts/research/tv_engine_odds.py deduplicates on (interval, broker_ts), so overlap costs nothing and buys a cross-shot consistency check on the shared bars. Like month-fill, these are wide reconciliation windows, NOT framed for candle-by-candle legibility.

month-legible.description: CH-visual-crt-state-fidelity: twenty M15 shots of 160 bars each with >=50-bar overlap, tiling the full 2,116-bar XAUUSD corpus at ~11 px/candle for per-candle visual labeling. Unlike month-fill / month-complete these ARE framed for candle-by-candle legibility. Run as one invocation so calibrate_clock runs once. Do not loosen frame_shot two-sided assertion; narrow and split on refusal.

h4_july_macro.name: 01_h4_july_macro
h4_july_macro.note: Screenshot 1 - full 4H July->August structure. Context only; no engine events mapped.

h4_july_setup.name: 02_h4_july_setup
h4_july_setup.note: Screenshot 2 - July 10 -> Jul 31 4H setup window. NOT CAPTURED as of 2026-08-17; no PNG or sidecar exists. END CORRECTED from 2026-08-01 23:45 to the Friday close: 2026-08-01 is a SATURDAY with zero bars on either feed, so the original right edge sat inside a market-closed gap. That correction did NOT fix the capture — the Jul 31 edge fails identically, so the Saturday edge was a real defect in this definition but NOT the cause of the framing failure (an in-session hypothesis, corrected rather than left standing). MEASURED failure: frame_shot's two-sided assertion refuses the result because the chart frames 2026-07-09 21:00..2026-08-02 21:00 — ~2 days wider at the right than requested — on BOTH the widget-API and --via-ui paths, which rules out the API path as the cause. Not a coverage loss: this window is a strict subset of 01_h4_july_macro (Jul 1 -> Aug 7), which DID capture and reconcile. The assertion was deliberately not loosened; it is the guard that caught shot 04's original mis-framing. Root cause (likely TradingView's bar-index range arithmetic over weekend gaps at this span) is UNRESOLVED and left open rather than worked around.
